name: decision

density.note: each option's tradeoff in a sentence or two

split.note: Verdict on an accent cover → justifications windowed. lib/core/carousel.js.

description: The verdict slide — one chosen path, named explicitly.
purpose: Use after a comparison slide to land the decision. The justifications render as one unified categorical strip — co-equal cards that together signal a single resolved verdict; the heading carries the decision, not a focal/subordinated split.

options.description: List items. Authoring contract: a top-level bullet is the option name (renders bold by default); an indented bullet underneath carries the short rationale. The cards render as a unified strip of co-equal categorical tags; the verdict is carried by the heading, not by emphasizing one card.

skeleton:
<!-- _class: decision -->

## What we are doing.

- Chosen path
  - One-line rationale for the decision.
- Rejected option
  - One-line rationale for why this didn't fit.
sample:
<!-- _class: decision -->

## The decision slide names the chosen path.

- The pick, stated plainly.
  - The chosen option leads with the verdict treatment and the reason it won, in one breath.
- The road not taken.
  - The alternative keeps its honest case — a decision against a straw man persuades no one.

stressDoc.sample:
<!-- _class: decision -->

## A verdict can carry two full arguments, no more.

- The chosen path, fully argued.
  - At the hard budget the winning card states the call, the strongest reason, and the accepted cost in two sentences — everything else belongs in the appendix.
- The alternative, fully respected.
  - The losing card may run just as long; a verdict earns trust precisely when the rejected option is shown at its strongest and still loses.

whenToUse.title: Land the verdict
whenToUse.body: Follows a comparison slide to make the chosen path unambiguous. The heading carries the verb of the decision; the cards substantiate it.

whenToUse.title: Two to four justifications
whenToUse.body: Each card is one short rationale — the chosen path first, then a Why-not card for each rejected alternative. More than four crowds the horizontal strip.

whenToUse.title: After the comparison
whenToUse.body: Pair with `compare-prose` or `split-compare` upstream — that slide does the weighing, this slide lands the answer. Reaching for decision without a prior comparison reads as edict.

antiPatterns.title: No clear chosen path
antiPatterns.body: If the cards don't resolve to a single verdict, the slide is back to being a comparison. Use `compare-prose` or `split-compare`; reserve decision for the resolved call.

antiPatterns.title: Long body per card
antiPatterns.body: Each card is one sentence of rationale. Paragraphs belong on the comparison slide upstream, not on the verdict slide.

antiPatterns.title: Generic heading
antiPatterns.body: The h2 carries the decision verb — Build, not buy. Adopt the framework. Pause the rollout. A heading like Next steps wastes the focal real estate.

related.name: compare-prose
related.when: the comparison slide that should precede decision

related.name: split-compare
related.when: comparison and verdict on one slide instead of two

related.name: closing
related.when: the deck ends without a single-call verdict

related.name: big-number
related.when: the decision is a quantitative commitment

banner-tag.label: banner-tag
banner-tag.summary: Headlines each card with its camp.
banner-tag.sample:
<!-- _class: decision banner-tag -->

## banner-tag headlines each card with its camp.

- DECIDE
  - The banner carries the stance; the body carries the reason.
- RECORD
  - Use when the slide is the decision log's public face.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reordering justification cards, expecting their categorical accent color to travel with the same justification.
commonMistakes.fix: The accent color is assigned purely by card POSITION (an `nth-child` cycle through the categorical palette), not by content — reordering cards in the markdown reassigns colors; they don't follow the justification.

commonMistakes.mistake: Manually bolding the option name with `**…**`.
commonMistakes.fix: The lead text auto-lifts to `<strong>` (the corner-tag CSS keys off it) — wrapping it yourself just nests a redundant, no-op bold marker.

variantDecisionRule.useWhen: The reasoning carries the weight — a quiet corner tag labels each justification without competing with the verdict heading.
The camp or stance itself is worth headlining — converts the quiet corner tag into a full-width banner strip per card.
